assumptions: Field labels (holder offsets, chunk size, inner size rule) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
The slot-bound reading (cursor runs while cursor < [holder+0x48] + 8, so the slot at [holder+0x48] itself is freed) is the observed unsigned comparison, not a claim about a source-level end pointer.
The inner-size reading ([holder+0x08] qwords, freed at count * 8) is the observed shift-and-delete; its source-level meaning is an inference, not a pinned fact.
The chunk and inner ranges are treated as well-formed; a corrupt range is not modelled.
behavior: Chunked array teardown: load inner = [holder]; a null inner returns plainly with nothing freed. Otherwise walk the holder's chunk-pointer slots from [holder+0x28] while the cursor is below [holder+0x48] + 8 (unsigned), stepping 8: free each slot's pointer with a sized delete of exactly 0x200 through the _ZdlPvm PLT at 0x63f0d80, with no null test on slot pointers. After the loop (or when it is skipped at entry), tail-jump to the same PLT freeing the inner object at ([holder+0x00], [holder+0x08] * 8). The holder itself is never freed, and no canary check is performed.

chunk_phase.null_slot_test: none; every slot pointer is passed to the sized delete

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

exits.condition: inner non-null, chunk phase done or skipped
exits.target: sized-delete PLT 0x63f0d80 freeing the inner object at ([holder+0x00], [holder+0x08] * 8)
